gloss: to be thorough; to be attentive; to reach everywhere

definitions.gloss: to be thorough; to be attentive; to be well looked after
definitions.explanation: Said of care, attention, or management that extends to every corner of something. Most often used in the ている form to describe a place, service, or piece of work as impeccably tended.

examples.japanese: {掃除|そうじ}が{行|い}き{届|とど}いている。
examples.english: The cleaning has been done thoroughly.

examples.japanese: この{旅館|りょかん}はサービスが{行|い}き{届|とど}いている。
examples.english: The service at this inn is attentive in every detail.

examples.japanese: {手入|てい}れの{行|い}き{届|とど}いた{庭|にわ}を{見|み}ると{気持|きも}ちがいい。
examples.english: It feels good to look at a well-tended garden.

examples.japanese: {生徒|せいと}の{数|かず}が{多|おお}すぎて、{一人|ひとり}ひとりに{指導|しどう}が{行|い}き{届|とど}かない。
examples.english: There are too many students, so instruction cannot reach every one of them.

notes:
A compound of {行|い}く (to go) + {届|とど}く (to reach). The subject is the care or attention itself, marked with が, not the person providing it.

ASPECT (ている):
The plain form is rare in the present tense. The normal affirmative use is {行|い}き{届|とど}いている (is thorough, is well looked after), a resulting state, while the negative {行|い}き{届|とど}かない points out where care is falling short.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {掃除|そうじ}が{行|い}き{届|とど}いている: is spotlessly clean
- サービスが{行|い}き{届|とど}いている: the service is attentive
- {手入|てい}れの{行|い}き{届|とど}いた: well-tended (as a modifier)
- {目|め}が{行|い}き{届|とど}く: to keep an eye on everything

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive. It takes no direct object; the area covered is marked with に (すみずみに{行|い}き{届|とど}く, to reach every corner).
